A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PoGDiff research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite substantial reorganization and formatting changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on AgeDB, DigiFace, and VGGFace, including quantitative comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experiments and adds CIFAR-100 results and qualitative observations about sensitivity and computational efficiency.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the final objective in Eq. (13) retain the same neighbor sampling, image-similarity weighting, inverse VAE-density weighting, and denoising loss. New VAE details and suggestions for obtaining missing class labels do not establish a changed implemented method.

E1.justification: v3 adds training and evaluation on CIFAR-100-IT2I, substantially extending coverage from facial identities to general object categories. AgeDB small, medium, and large, DigiFace, and VGGFace remain; AgeDB-medium results move into the full-results appendix.

E2.justification: Vanilla Stable Diffusion, CBDM, and T2H remain the evaluated comparators, including on CIFAR-100. T2H is recharacterized as feature augmentation rather than reweighting, but its documented adaptation using text-embedding density remains unchanged.

E3.justification: Existing stated face-evaluation protocols remain unchanged. The added CIFAR experiment introduces imbalance ratio 250, majority downsampling, Inception-v3 FID features, and training for 24,000 steps at learning rate 0.0001 with effective batch size 128. Appendix J.8 also describes a matched-time comparison of 12,000 SD steps against 6,000 PoGDiff steps.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 6 and existing t-SNE and qualitative analyses are retained. Appendices J.7–J.8 add brief, unquantified reports of sensitivity to VAE architecture, learning rate, and training duration, plus an equal-time training comparison.

E5.justification: Both main texts describe ten generation seeds, and both evaluation appendices average ten GPT-4o ratings per image. Neither adds training-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new checklist calls error bars inapplicable without changing the reporting practice.

E6.justification: Existing face-benchmark and ablation scores are retained, while v3 adds CIFAR results across all five metrics. For example, Table 1 reports PoGDiff FID 6.24/9.41 versus Vanilla 7.19/11.46 for all/few-shot evaluation. These are new-domain results, not improvements on retained experiments. One new entry is ambiguous: Table 8 prints T2H's CIFAR DINO value as '0345', whereas Table 2 gives 0.45.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.1 revises the stated Gaussian means from noise quantities epsilon_theta and epsilon to x_theta and x_{t-1}. This is a limited mathematical formulation revision. Proposition 3.1, its precision assumption, the Appendix A proof, and the gRecall definition remain unchanged; the new convergence discussion supplies no formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: a general PoGDiff approach for imbalanced text-to-image generation, its objective interpretation, the gRecall contribution, and superiority over the evaluated baselines. Additional benchmark evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendices J.6–J.9 add informal convergence reasoning, discussion of obtaining unavailable class labels, and an Einstein/Charlie Ruggles example explaining identity errors through overlapping prompt traits. They also interpret small identity deviations as potentially beneficial for diversity. Earlier limitations and FID interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents VGGFace training settings, CIFAR settings, three-layer MLP VAE encoders and decoders, approximate VAE training time, and relative training/inference costs. VGGFace settings are newly disclosed rather than demonstrably changed. The checklist also announces code release after acceptance; it does not establish current availability.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Kim et al. on unbiased diffusion, Choi et al. on fair generative modeling, and Cao et al. for the long-tailed dataset setting. It expands the short related-work discussion and recharacterizes T2H, while retaining the original positioning against class-conditioned diffusion and customization methods.

P1.justification: The document is substantially reorganized: dataset construction, ablations, full benchmark results, FID interpretation, and the impact statement are redistributed into appendices, while baseline descriptions expand in the main text. New discussion subsections and a NeurIPS checklist are added. Much underlying prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two columns to one, with extensive resizing and relocation of displays. Main result tables substitute CIFAR columns for AgeDB-medium, while expanded appendix tables preserve full coverage. Dataset-distribution plots are consolidated and extended, and the main qualitative image grid is shortened from ten to eight rows.

improvement.justification: CIFAR-100 adds useful evidence beyond the earlier exclusively facial evaluation, while new implementation, computational-cost, and failure-case details improve transparency. The gains are limited: sensitivity and equal-time findings remain qualitative, and the new CIFAR human/GPT scores retain face-specific evaluation descriptions. These additions modestly strengthen the paper without substantially resolving its evidential limitations.
